name: Observation of a charged charmoniumlike structure in e+e- to pi+pi-J/psi at sqrt(s)=4.26 GeV
notes: The same structure was reported by Belle shortly afterwards (not recorded here).

summary.plain: BESIII studied electron-positron collisions at 4.26 GeV that make a pion pair and a J/psi, and saw a structure near 3.9 GeV in the pion-J/psi mass. Called Zc(3900), it is unusual in that it carries an electric charge and couples to charmonium.
summary.technical: BESIII: e⁺e⁻ → π⁺π⁻J/ψ at √s = 4.260 GeV with 525 pb⁻¹; Born cross section (62.9 ± 1.9 ± 3.7) pb consistent with Y(4260) production; a structure at about 3.9 GeV/c² in the π^±J/ψ mass spectrum, the Zc(3900), with M = (3899.0 ± 3.6 ± 4.9) MeV/c² and Γ = (46 ± 10 ± 20) MeV; 'if interpreted as a new particle, it is unusual in that it carries an electric charge and couples to charmonium'.

title: Observation of a charged charmoniumlike structure in e+e- to pi+pi-J/psi at sqrt(s)=4.26 GeV
why_it_matters: The abstract notes that, if it is a new particle, it is unusual in that it carries an electric charge and couples to charmonium.
